---
title: "SPEC-v0.3.0"
subtitle: "The templates, the shared rules, pending work and yrNewAiProject, version 0.3.0"
---

## Purpose {#sec-purpose}

Every new project for AI-assisted work starts from the same base:

- rules that every AI agent and every collaborator reads;
- a Quarto book of project documents;
- a skill to add documents;
- a list of pending work (things to do later), kept as GitHub issues.

There are two types of project: `work` and `book`. One command, `yrNewAiProject.sh`, makes a project, and it
checks a project against its template. The user guide (`USER-GUIDE-v001.qmd`) tells how to use them. This SPEC
says what they must do.

## Changes from SPEC-v0.2.0 {#sec-changes}

- Template v0.3.0: every project has the `pending-work` skill and a SessionStart hook in `.claude/settings.json`
  that shows the user how many pending items are open (@sec-pending). `AGENTS.md` has a "Pending work" section.
- `yrNewAiProject --github` also makes the labels of the pending-work skill (@sec-tool-make).
- `agents-init --pending-work` adds the skill and the hook to an existing project (@sec-pending-existing).
- `yrNewAiProject --preview` and `agents-init --diff` show what the tools would do to an existing folder, and
  change nothing (@sec-tool-preview).
- `yrNewAiProject` is version 0.3.0. Template v0.2.0 does not change.

## Repository layout {#sec-layout}

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `templates/vX.Y.Z/shared/` | Files for every project of that version |
| `templates/vX.Y.Z/TYPE/` | Files for one type (`work`, `book`; `generic` in v0.0.1) |
| `rules/AGENTS.md` | The shared rules: the text from its first `## ` heading on |
| `bin/yrNewAiProject.py`, `bin/agents_init.py` | The tools (Python 3.8 or later, standard library only) |
| `bin/setup-computer.sh` | The setup of one computer |
| `tests/selftest.py` | The tests |
| `docs/` | This book |

The commands `yrNewAiProject.sh` and `agents-init.sh` are wrappers in the Dropbox tools folder. Each one finds the
repository by a path relative to its own folder (`../_yrAiCoding/yrAiProjectTemplates`). Each one runs the Python
script with the first of `python3`, `python` and `py -3` that runs Python 3.8 or later.

## Template versions {#sec-versions}

1. A version folder name is `v` and three numbers. The newest version (highest numbers) is the default.
2. A version is released when the repository has the git tag `templates-vX.Y.Z`. The files of a released
   version must not change. A change goes into a new version folder, which has its own SPEC.
3. The type folders of a version are its types. The `shared` folder is not a type.

## Project contents in v0.3.0 {#sec-contents}

| File | `work` | `book` |
|---|---|---|
| `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.gitignore` | yes | yes |
| `README.md` | the work README | the book README |
| `docs/_quarto.yml`, `docs/index.qmd`, `docs/.gitignore` | yes | yes (the book's `_quarto.yml` also lists the PLANNING document) |
| `docs/SPEC-v0.1.0.qmd`, `docs/TODO-v001.qmd` | yes | yes |
| `docs/DOC-GUIDE-v001.qmd`, `docs/QUARTO-GUIDE-v001.qmd` | yes | yes |
| `docs/PLANNING-v001.qmd` | no | yes |
| `.claude/skills/pending-work/SKILL.md`, `scripts/pending.sh` | yes | yes |
| `.claude/settings.json` (the SessionStart hook) | yes | yes |
| `_quarto.yml`, `index.qmd`, `intro.qmd` (the main book) | no | yes |
| `.claude/skills/new-doc/SKILL.md`, `new_doc.py` | yes | yes |
| `.yrAiProjectTemplate/manifest.json` | yes | yes |

Each `.gitignore` of a book folder holds the exact line `/.quarto/`. Without that line, Quarto adds it at the first
render, and the project would then have an uncommitted change.

## Placeholders {#sec-placeholders}

| Form | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `{{YRAI:KEY}}` | A value that the tool fills in. `KEY` is capital letters, digits and `_` |
| `<!-- YRAI:BEGIN:NAME -->` ... `<!-- YRAI:END:NAME -->` | A region that the user writes. The markers stay in the file |
| `{{YRAI:BEGIN:NAME}}` ... `{{YRAI:END:NAME}}` | The region form of v0.0.1, still read by `--check-content` |

The tool fills these values:

| Key | Value |
|---|---|
| `PROJECT_NAME` | The folder name |
| `PROJECT_TITLE` | `--title`, or the folder name |
| `PROJECT_DESCRIPTION` | `--description`, or a TODO line |
| `PROJECT_TYPE` | The type |
| `CREATED_DATE` | The date, `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `TEMPLATE_VERSION` | The version, `vX.Y.Z` |

1. In `.yml` files, and in the YAML front matter of `.qmd` and `.md` files, a template puts each value in double
   quotes. The tool escapes `\` and `"` in those values.
2. A key that the tool does not know stays as it is.
3. A file that is not UTF-8 text is copied unchanged.

## The shared rules {#sec-rules}

1. The shared block is the text of `rules/AGENTS.md` from its first `## ` heading on.
2. In a project's `AGENTS.md`, the block is between a line that starts with `<!-- begin shared rules` and the line
   `<!-- end shared rules -->`. `agents_init.update()` replaces the text between them, and keeps the rest of the
   file. If the markers are missing, it adds the block at the end.
3. `agents_init.update()` also makes sure that `CLAUDE.md` has the line `@AGENTS.md`. It adds the line at the top,
   or creates the file. It does not write through a symlink.
4. `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` on the owner's computers imports `rules/AGENTS.md`.

## The manifest {#sec-manifest}

`.yrAiProjectTemplate/manifest.json`, schema 2:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 2,
  "templateVersion": "v0.3.0",
  "projectType": "work",
  "values": {"PROJECT_NAME": "...", "PROJECT_TITLE": "...", "PROJECT_DESCRIPTION": "...",
             "PROJECT_TYPE": "work", "CREATED_DATE": "2026-10-12", "TEMPLATE_VERSION": "v0.3.0"},
  "createdAt": "2026-10-12T18:00:00Z",
  "addedToExisting": false,
  "installer": {"name": "yrNewAiProject", "version": "0.3.0"},
  "metaRepo": {"path": "/home/.../yrAiProjectTemplates", "commit": "abc1234"}
}
```

`--verify` also reads schema 1, the manifest of `yraiproject`. It reads that manifest as version
`v<templateVersion>`, type `generic`, with no values.

## yrNewAiProject {#sec-tool}

### Make a project {#sec-tool-make}

1. The target folder must not exist, or be empty, or hold only `.git`. With `--strict-empty`, `.git` alone is
   refused. Otherwise: exit 3, and nothing is written.
2. With `--add-to-existing`, the folder can hold files. If a template file, or the manifest, exists already, the
   tool lists the files, writes nothing, and exits with status 4.
3. With `--github`: the tool first checks that `gh` exists and is logged in (else exit 2). `--github` with
   `--add-to-existing` is refused (exit 2), because there is no first commit to push.
4. The tool copies the `shared` files, then the type files (a type file replaces a shared file with the same path).
   It skips `.git`, `__pycache__`, `.quarto`, `_book`, `.DS_Store` and `yraiproject.template.yml`. It fills in the
   values in text files, and it keeps the file permissions.
5. It fills in the shared rules (@sec-rules), then writes the manifest.
6. If the folder has no `.git`, it runs `git init -b main`. Without `--add-to-existing`, it commits all the files
   ("Make NAME from yrAiProjectTemplates VERSION (TYPE project)"). A git failure: exit 5.
7. With `--github`, it runs `gh repo create NAME --private --source PATH --remote origin --push`. A failure: exit
   5. The local project stays. If the project has `.claude/skills/pending-work/scripts/pending.sh`, it then runs
   `pending.sh setup-labels`. A failure there is a warning, not an error.
8. `--dry-run` lists the files and the actions, and changes nothing.

### Check a project {#sec-tool-verify}

1. `--verify PATH` reads the manifest (no manifest: exit 2). `--type` and `--version` replace its values.
2. A template file that is missing is a problem. A file that is not from the template (outside `.git`, the
   skipped names and the manifest) is a note. Shared rules that are out of date are a note.
3. With `--check-content`, the tool fills the template file with the manifest values, and compares it with the
   project file. The YRAI regions, the keys without a value and the shared-rules block can hold any text. Any other
   difference is a problem. Line ends `\r\n` and `\n` are the same. A binary file must be the same, byte for byte.
4. Exit 1 if there is a problem, else 0.

### Preview an existing folder {#sec-tool-preview}

`--preview PATH` changes nothing. `PATH` must be a folder (else exit 2). The type is `--type`, or `book` if `PATH`
has `_quarto.yml`, else `work`. The report has two parts:

1. What `--add-to-existing` would do. Each template file that exists already is listed and marked "same as the
   template" (the same text, with the values filled in) or "differs from the template"; an existing manifest is
   listed too. If anything is listed, the report says that the tool would stop with exit 4 and write nothing. Then
   it lists the template files that would be added.
2. What `agents-init --pending-work` would do: the output of `agents-init --diff --pending-work` (below).

Exit 0. `--preview` with `--verify`: exit 2.

`agents-init --diff [--pending-work] [DIR]` changes nothing. For each file that agents-init would create or change
(`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and, with `--pending-work`, `.claude/settings.json`) it prints a unified diff, and it
lists the skill files that it would add. Exit 0. `--diff` with `--check`: an error.

### Other {#sec-tool-other}

`--list` lists the versions, newest first, with their types. `-h` and `--help` print the help (the docstring) and
exit 0. Bad options: exit 2.

## The new-doc skill {#sec-documents}

1. Document types are names in capital letters, digits and hyphens. The default is `SPEC`. There are no PRDs.
2. A SPEC file is `SPEC-vX.Y.Z.qmd`. The default version is the newest SPEC's version with the last number plus 1,
   or `0.1.0` if there is no SPEC. `--version` gives another one.
3. Another type's file is `TYPE-vNNN.qmd`, with the next copy number (`001` first).
4. The new file is a copy of the newest version of its type, with the new title. With `--blank`, or when there is
   no older version, it is the outline of the type.
5. The script lists the file in `docs/_quarto.yml`: above the newest older version of the type; else at the end of
   its part (`Specification` for SPEC, `Guides` for a name that ends in `GUIDE`, else `Work`, or `--part`); else in
   a new part at the end of `book: chapters:`.
6. A file that exists is never replaced.

## Pending work {#sec-pending}

Pending items are things to do later. The user talks to the agent; the agent does the GitHub work.

1. An item is a GitHub issue in the project's repository (the `origin` remote) with the label `pending-work`, one
   category label (by default `fix`, `improvement`, `decision` or `recheck`) and one priority label
   (`priority: high`, `priority: medium` or `priority: low`).
2. `scripts/pending.sh` needs only bash and `gh` (it uses the jq that is built into `gh`), so it also runs in Git
   Bash on Windows. Its commands:

   | Command | What it does |
   |---|---|
   | `session-start` | Prints the JSON for the SessionStart hook (below) |
   | `list` | The open items, one per line (`#12 [high] Title  (category)`), highest priority first |
   | `export` | Writes the open items, with their text, to `_pending-work/pendingWork.md` |
   | `setup-labels` | Makes or updates the labels (safe to repeat) |
   | `-h`, `--help` | Prints the help and stops |

   The settings at the top of the script, `MIRROR`, `QUEUE` and `CATEGORIES`, may be changed for a project. The
   folder `_pending-work/` starts with `_`, so Quarto does not render it.
3. `.claude/settings.json` runs `pending.sh session-start` for the SessionStart sources `startup` and `clear`. The
   output is JSON with:
   - `systemMessage`, which the user sees: the count by priority, for example `Pending work: 12 pending items (3
     high, 5 medium, 4 low). Want to see them? Say "list pending".`, or `Pending work: nothing pending.`;
   - `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`, which the agent gets: the same count and how to answer. **It does not
     hold the list**, so that the list uses no context until the user asks for it.
4. When `gh` is missing or not logged in, GitHub cannot be reached, or the project has no GitHub remote,
   `session-start` and `list` use the saved copy (`_pending-work/pendingWork.md`) and the items that the agent
   queued in `_pending-work/queue.md` (headings `### [priority] Title`). The output says that the count may be out
   of date.
5. `SKILL.md` tells the agent how to show, add, change, work on and close items, and how to handle the queue.

### Add pending work to an existing project {#sec-pending-existing}

`agents-init --pending-work [DIR]`:

1. copies the files of `.claude/skills/pending-work/` from the `shared/` folder of the newest template version
   that has them. A file that exists is never replaced (the project may have changed the settings in
   `pending.sh`);
2. adds the SessionStart entry of that version's `.claude/settings.json` to the project's `.claude/settings.json`,
   unless a SessionStart entry already runs `pending.sh`. The other settings are kept. A file that is not valid JSON
   is not changed (the tool stops with a message). If the project has no settings file, it is created;
3. with `--check`, changes nothing, and exits with status 1 if a skill file or the hook is missing.

## Tests {#sec-tests}

`tests/selftest.py` makes test projects in a scratch folder and checks every function in this SPEC. It also
checks every error status, that a Quarto render leaves no uncommitted change, the output of
`pending.sh session-start` (with no GitHub repository, so it needs no network), `agents-init --pending-work`, and
that `--preview` and `agents-init --diff` change nothing. GitHub Actions runs it and
renders this book on each push. It never runs `--github` without `--dry-run`.
